paragraphs: Rabbi Abba son of Rav Yitzchak, Menachot 106a.
In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 12:1 he is called Rabbi Ba. Rav Ada son of Rav Yitzchak, Yoma 17a.
Rav Acha son of Yitzchak, Shabbat ch. 3, halakhah 4.
Rav Dimi son of Yitzchak, Megillah 10b.
Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Yitzchak, Avodah Zarah 33b.
Rav Chanan-Chinena-Chanina son of Yitzchak, Berakhot ch. 6, halakhah 1. Tuvia son of Yitzchak, Eruvin 28b.
Rav Nachman son of Yitzchak, Berakhot 5b. Rava son of Yitzchak, Sotah 46b. Rabbah son of Yitzchak, Yevamot 71b.
Rav Shila son of Yitzchak, the old Midrash Tehillim, chapter 91.
Rav Shmuel son of Rav Yitzchak, Berakhot 31b.

notes.text: The heading and checked Yoma passage support Yitzchak in the abbreviated patronymic. “The old Midrash Tehillim” is retained as Hyman’s description without assigning a particular edition. This is a collective list.

The consulted Yoma 17a explicitly names Rav Ada son of Rav Yitzchak. The heading is a collective patronymic list, not proof that all the listed men shared one father. Hyman’s “old Midrash Tehillim” description is retained without assigning an independently uninspected exact edition.
